guide.h2: Choosing a carpet cleaner in Leeds
p: Carpet cleaning in Leeds ranges from one person businesses with a van mounted machine to larger firms with several teams. A good carpet cleaner will ask about the fibre, the age of the carpet and any stains before quoting, because wool, polypropylene and natural fibres need different treatment.

Look for a professional carpet cleaning firm that explains its cleaning method, gives a written price and is insured. Google reviews that mention specific stains, pets or drying times are more useful than a star rating on its own.

ul: Hot water extraction (often called steam cleaning): a hot cleaning solution is sprayed into the carpet and extracted. It gives a deep clean but takes longer to dry, often several hours.
Low moisture cleaning: uses less water and dries faster, useful for offices or homes that need the room back the same day.
Spot and stain treatment: specific products for wine, coffee, grease, pet urine and odour. Not every stain comes out, and a good cleaner will say so before starting.

p: Most carpet cleaners in Leeds also clean sofas, armchairs, mattresses and rugs. Check the care label on your sofa first: a code of W means water based cleaning is fine, S means solvent only. Delicate fabrics such as velvet or silk are best left to a specialist.

guide.h2: How much does carpet cleaning cost?
p: Prices are usually per room, per stair flight or per item for sofas. Ask for a fixed price before the clean, and check whether stain treatment and deodorising are included or extra. Checkatrade's 2026 guide puts a small to medium room at about £50, stairs and landing at about £85 and a three bedroom home at about £250, with minimum charges of around £85 a visit. See our carpet cleaning cost guide.

guide.h2: End of tenancy carpet cleaning in Leeds
p: Landlords and letting agents in Leeds often expect carpets to be professionally cleaned when a tenancy ends, especially in student areas such as Headingley and Hyde Park. Check your tenancy agreement, keep the receipt and take dated photos after the clean in case of a deposit dispute.

guide.h2: Questions to ask a carpet cleaner
ul: Which cleaning method will you use, and how long will it take to dry?
Is the price fixed, and does it include stain treatment?
Are you insured if something is damaged?
Do you need parking near the door for a van mounted machine?
What happens if a stain does not come out?

faqs.q: How long does a carpet take to dry after cleaning?
faqs.a: After hot water extraction, usually several hours, and longer in cold or damp weather. Low moisture methods can be dry in an hour or two. Open windows and keep the heating on to speed it up.

faqs.q: Is professional carpet cleaning worth it?
faqs.a: For heavily used, stained or smelly carpets, yes. A professional machine extracts far more dirt and water than a hire machine, so the carpet dries faster and stays clean longer.

faqs.q: Can carpet cleaners remove pet urine smells?
faqs.a: Often, but not always. Fresh accidents usually clean well. Old urine that has soaked into the underlay may need the underlay treated or replaced.

faqs.q: Do I need to move furniture before the carpet cleaner arrives?
faqs.a: Ask the firm. Many will move light furniture, but you should clear small items, breakables and anything on the floor.

faqs.q: Is it worth cleaning an old carpet?
faqs.a: If it is worn through or the backing is breaking up, a clean will not fix it. If the pile is still intact, a clean can make an older carpet look much better.
